query: We have a Python microservice at `~/repos/order-gateway/src/external_clients/` that fans out requests to five third-party supplier APIs (inventory check, pricing, tax calculation, fraud scoring, and shipping estimation) before assembling a consolidated order quote. Right now if any one of those calls fails or hangs, the whole quote request blows up and the customer gets a 500. I need you to build a robust `resilient_client.py` module that wraps our existing `httpx.AsyncClient` calls with: (1) per-supplier configurable timeouts (connect vs. read vs. total), (2) a retry layer with exponential backoff plus jitter that respects each supplier's rate-limit headers (`Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`), (3) a circuit breaker that trips open after N consecutive failures and periodically half-opens to probe recovery, and (4) a fallback strategy per supplier (e.g., return cached pricing, skip fraud scoring with a flag, use a default flat-rate shipping estimate). The retries should distinguish between transient errors (429, 502, 503, 504, `ConnectTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`) and permanent ones (400, 401, 404) that should fail immediately. Also include structured logging so we can trace every attempt, backoff delay, circuit state transition, and fallback activation per request-id. Write tests using `pytest` + `respx` that simulate flaky suppliers — random latency spikes, intermittent 503 bursts, rate-limit responses — and assert that the module converges to a successful quote within the configured budget of time and retries rather than cascading failures.

query: We have a FastAPI service called "IngestHub" that accepts webhook payloads from third-party IoT sensors and fans them out to downstream processors. query: Design an autonomous iOS agent in Swift that monitors our app "TypeCraft" (a typography education tool) and automatically adjusts all text elements to comply with Apple's Human Interface Guidelines for iOS 26 — specifically San Francisco font usage, Dynamic Type scaling, proper tracking/leading values per text style (Large Title, Body, Caption, etc.), and correct optical sizing. The agent should run a continuous ReAct-style loop: observe the current screen hierarchy, reason about which labels/text views deviate from the HIG spec (wrong point size for a given text style, incorrect tracking at a specific optical size, missing Dynamic Type support, improper leading for a locale like Arabic or Thai), plan corrective actions, apply fixes via our internal styling API, then verify the changes actually rendered correctly by re-inspecting the view hierarchy. It needs goal decomposition so it can break "make all typography HIG-compliant" into subtasks per screen, a reflection/self-correction mechanism so that if a fix causes truncation or accessibility regressions it rolls back and tries an alternative approach, and a reliability strategy to handle the compounding error problem — if it's checking 40+ screens with dozens of text elements each, one bad decision shouldn't cascade. Include exponential backoff on failed corrections, confidence thresholds for when to apply changes autonomously vs. flag for human review, and structured logging of every observe-think-act cycle. Make sure the tracking table matches the iOS 26 San Francisco specifications exactly (e.g., Body at 17pt with 0.0 tracking, Caption2 at 11pt with +0.07 tracking, etc.) and that the agent handles SF Pro, SF Pro Rounded, SF Mono, and SF Compact variants correctly.

I also want tests that confirm two calls with the same ID always produce identical output and that different IDs produce distinct fingerprints with high probability.
